Oral medicine and dentistry · published research

COVID-19 related oral lesions

Uncontrolled reports describe improvement in oral lesions, often after combined PBM and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy. They do not establish an independent PBM effect.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Uncontrolled reports describe improvement in oral lesions, often after combined PBM and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy. They do not establish an independent PBM effect.

Summary of the Evidence

Four primary human publications are indexed under COVID-19 oral symptoms (two case reports and two case series; the series include 3 and 4 cases), plus a meta-analysis of 11 cases across five articles. The synthesis reuses case literature and is not an additional cohort count. No controlled trial or preclinical study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

Uncontrolled reports describe lesion or symptom improvement after PBM, often combined with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT); one case report used PBM after mouthwashes, with laser parameters unreported. Concomitant therapies, case-level samples, and mixed PBM/aPDT protocols prevent attribution of benefit to PBM alone (Chaughtai et al., 2022; Sachet et al. 2022; Teixeira et al. 2021; do Vale Castro et al., 2024; Pacheco et al., 2022). These publications describe acute infection-associated lesions and mixed protocols; they do not show that PBM treats SARS-CoV-2 infection itself or prevents post-COVID oral symptoms. Use of antimicrobial photodynamic therapy in some cases further complicates attribution, and the case synthesis should not be added to the primary case count.

Primary original study: Teixeira et al. 2021 multicenter series: Sachet et al. 2022

Animal evidence

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The case literature uses different light sources and commonly combines PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy. The reports do not establish a standardized dose across cases, and no common parameter set is inferred. Visible red or blue wavelengths, when used, are distinct from near-infrared wavelengths; outcomes from mixed protocols cannot be transferred between them.

Interpretation

These reports describe care for oral lesions in people with COVID-19, not treatment of SARS-CoV-2 infection itself. Concurrent therapies, spontaneous recovery, and the lack of comparators prevent causal attribution. The case synthesis should be kept separate from primary reports to avoid counting the same patients twice.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. Case reports and series often combine PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy.
Publications and records5 unique titles: 4 primary human reports and 1 synthesis of overlapping case literature.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The available primary reports are case reports and small case series, often combining PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy or other care. A synthesis of reported cases reuses this literature and is not an independent cohort. There are no controlled trials establishing that PBM caused lesion improvement or altered COVID-19 infection outcomes.
